title: Second moment of restricted Fourier coefficients
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $S\subseteq J$. For each fixed assignment $z\in\{-1,1\}^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus J}$, take the Fourier coefficient of the restriction of $f$ to the coordinates in $J$, at frequency $S$. The uniform expectation over $z$ of the square of this coefficient equals the sum, over all subsets $T$ of the complementary coordinates, of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ at frequency $S\cup T$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
$J$ is a subset of the coordinates
